newsitem.title: FRANCE: French capital markets closing report.
newsitem.headline: French capital markets closing report.

text.p: French interest rate futures came under pressure during an otherwise torpid session from non-residents after two opinion polls published during the weekend showed the left gaining ground on the ruling coalition.
The June contract tumbled seven basis points to 96.35, just above an area of support at 96.34, although traders said the volume was fairly limited with only 13,000 lots traded.

A futures trader at a French bank said while there had been pressure on Monday, he would only be concerned if a poll suggested the left would secure more seats than the ruling coalition in the May 25/June 1 parliamentary election.

Bond traders said it was very quiet and the fact the LIFFE Bund future was closed for a bank holiday helped reduce the volume on the French bond future to 26,699 lots, its lowest daily volume this year and less than a tenth of its busiest day.
"It's total standby. Nothing happened," another trader said. "Now we're waiting for the Louis Harris poll later today."

The decline in PIBOR was largely expected by most analysts who have been saying for several days French interest rate futures were not pricing a large enough risk premium even though the most likely outcome was still a centre-right victory.

"Only the very short end of the yield curve has posted some signs of caution...neither the long end nor the currency market are impressed" by the risk of a left-wing victory, Eric Chaney at Morgan Stanley in Paris said.

The June bond future settled virtually unchanged at 129.50 on Monday although it lagged the DTB Bund contract slightly, bringing in the 10-year yield spread to minus seven from minus nine basis points on Friday.
The franc slipped slightly along with PIBOR to a low of 3.3758 against the mark on Monday and was at 3.3742 late in the session, down from 3.3717 on Friday.
As expected the Bank of France left the intervention rate unchanged at 3.10 percent at a regular money market tender. Its monetary policy council meets on Wednesday.
The average yield on three-month bills was unchanged at auction on Monday and the Treasury said it would be selling 300 to 500 million Ecu of the benchmark 10-year OAT on Wednesday.
